findings.title: Fix is incomplete: paginated getSubGroupsStream variants still NPE on concurrent group deletion
findings.body: The PR fixes the NPE in getSubGroupsCount() by null-checking the lazily loaded delegate, but the same race still exists in the three sibling methods that also dereference modelSupplier.get() without a null check: getSubGroupsStream(String search, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 262), and getSubGroupsStream(String search, Boolean exact, Integer firstResult, Integer maxResults) (line 268). Each of these calls modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly, so if the group is concurrently deleted between the cache load and this call, the supplier returns null and a NullPointerException is still thrown. Since the PR's stated purpose is to fix NPEs when accessing a group concurrently, these paths need the same null handling (e.g., return Stream.empty() or delegate consistently) or the bug will simply resurface through the paginated subgroup endpoints.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so exceptions can be added after the assertion and silently missed
findings.body: createMultiDeleteMultiReadMulti starts a background thread that repeatedly lists groups and collects exceptions into caughtExceptions, sets deletedAll after the delete loop, and then immediately asserts caughtExceptions is empty (line 157). The thread is never joined: between deletedAll.set(true) and the assertion the reader thread can still be inside managedRealm.admin().groups().groups(...), and an exception thrown there (the very NPE this PR is fixing) is added to the list only after the assertion has already passed, so the test can green-light a failure it was written to catch. Conversely, if the delete loop itself throws, deletedAll is never set and the non-daemon reader thread spins in a tight HTTP loop forever, hanging the test JVM. The thread should be stored, and after deletedAll.set(true) the test should join() it (with a timeout) before asserting on caughtExceptions, ideally in a finally block so the thread is always terminated.
